title: Telemetry-Driven Prompt Surgeon and Repair Playbook
author: Asha Menon
content:
Summary
=======
This playbook defines the Prompt Surgeon framework: an operational, telemetry-driven process for automatically diagnosing, proposing, and (when safe) applying prompt-level repairs to production prompts that cause degraded quality after model or infra changes. The goal is to reduce time-to-remediation for prompt-driven regressions while preserving human-in-the-loop (HITL) safety and auditability.

Scope
-----
- Applies to customer-facing prompt sets used in Redwood-hosted and Dedicated runtimes (generation and chat endpoints).
- Focuses on regressions that originate from prompt-sensitivity: phrasing, tokenization, context size, exemplar placement, and instruction framing.
- Not a substitute for model rollback: actions are constrained to conservative, reversible prompt changes and controlled canaries.

Definitions
-----------
- Prompt Surgeon: automated system that suggests and tests minimal prompt edits.
- Trigger Event: alert from quality guardrails or eval harness indicating increased error rate or decline in response quality for a slice.
- Repair Candidate: a small, deterministic prompt modification (e.g., change to instruction, added anchor sentence, reordering of few-shot examples).
- Acceptance Criteria: quant thresholds for allowing an automatic rollout.

Signals and Telemetry (what to monitor)
--------------------------------------
- Quality Signals:
  - Slice F1 / BLEU / ROUGE for structured tasks (threshold: drop > 5% relative to baseline).
  - Semantic Similarity score distributions against golden responses (drift > 0.12 cosine).
  - Response Stability Index (RSI) — new metric: fraction of identical top-3 token choices across seeds (alert if RSI < 0.7).
- Operational Signals:
  - Latency P95 change associated with prompt length or added tokens (> +30ms correlated).
  - Token economy impact: median tokens per request changes > +10%.
- Telemetry sources: production traces (trace IDs), evaluator harness replays, user-reported misclassifications, and annotator labeling jobs.

Prompt Surgeon Workflow (high level)
------------------------------------
1) Detection
   - Guardrails alert on a Trigger Event. The triage pipeline attaches telemetry slices (customer, route, model version, prompt hash).
2) Isolation
   - Narrow to affected prompt templates or prompt clusters using prompt-fingerprint clustering (MinHash + semantic embedding clustering).
3) Candidate Synthesis
   - Generate repair candidates using:
     a) Minimal perturbations library (deterministic rewrites such as explicit anchoring sentences, clarification tokens).
     b) Learned paraphrase models constrained to n-token changes (beam width 5).
     c) Fallback heuristics (reduce context length, swap exemplar order).
   - Each candidate includes a stability score and a complexity score (tokens changed + syntactic edit distance).
4) Local Simulation and Eval Harness Replay
   - Run candidates through the eval harness in shadow mode across: production traffic traces, stratified prompt slices, and adversarial variants.
   - Record utility metrics (accuracy, semantic similarity), cost metrics (tokens, latency), and safety signals (toxic content checks).
5) Candidate Scoring and Prioritization
   - Score = weighted combination: quality_improvement*0.6 + cost_reduction*0.2 + rollback_risk_score*0.2.
   - Prioritize low-risk, high-improvement edits; tag those suitable for automated canary.
6) Human Validation (HITL)
   - For candidates above a threshold, create a triage card with: diff view, before/after examples, confidence bands, and suggested rollout plan.
   - Reviewer must sign-off for any candidate that changes instruction semantics or touches policy-sensitive wording.
7) Canary and Gradual Rollout
   - Canary on 1% traffic for 24–72 hours with automated rollback triggers (see Rollout section).
8) Promote or Revert
   - If acceptance criteria met, promote to 10% then 50% and 100% with checkpoints. Otherwise automatically revert and escalate.

Automated Repair Candidate Specification
----------------------------------------
- Format: {id, prompt_delta_plaintext, delta_tokens, rationale, categories, safe_flag}
- Example candidate (plain text):
  - id: PS-2025-0956
  - prompt_delta_plaintext: "Add anchor: \"When in doubt, provide a concise summary in 3 bullets.\" at top."
  - delta_tokens: +9
  - rationale: anchors instruction to enforce concision, reduces hallucination exposure on long context.
  - categories: ["anchor", "clarification"]
  - safe_flag: true

Safety, Audit, and Compliance
-----------------------------
- All automated edits are recorded in the Prompt Audit Log (service: prompt-audit-svc). Entries include diff, request/response samples, canary metrics, and human approver IDs.
- Policy-sensitive terms are flagged via the content-policy-checker; any candidate touching flagged terms requires reviewer approval.
- Retention: audit logs retained 3 years for customers on enterprise contracts; 90 days for standard.

Acceptance Criteria (must be programmatically checkable)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Quality improvement on affected slice >= +6% with p < 0.05 across 5 replay seeds.
- No regressions on 5 conservatively-chosen control slices (each slice delta >= -1%).
- Latency P95 change <= +5% absolute.
- Token cost change <= +5% absolute unless quality improvement > +10%.
- Safety checks: zero new moderate-or-higher toxicity flags in canary sample (n=500).

Rollout and Canary Triggers
--------------------------
- Canary duration: 24–72h depending on variance budget.
- Automated rollback triggers (any will trigger immediate revert):
  - Quality drop on any control slice > 2%.
  - Increase in user-reported error rate > 1.5x baseline in canary cohort.
  - Latency P95 increase > 15% from baseline in canary cohort.
- Manual rollback: reviewer can revert via console action or CLI:
  - CLI: redwood prompt-surgeon rollback --candidate PS-2025-0956 --reason "unexpected intent shift"

Metrics and Dashboards (what to surface)
----------------------------------------
- Candidate dashboard: top candidates, predicted impact, stability score, reviewer status.
- Canary dashboard: canary cohort metrics vs baseline (quality, latency, tokens, safety flags).
- Prompt Health Index (PHI): composite score (0–100) combining slice stability, error rate, and drift velocity. SLO: PHI >= 85 for production prompts.

Runbook: Immediate Steps on Trigger
----------------------------------
1) Acknowledge alert and review the triage summary in the Playbook UI.
2) If root cause is prompt sensitivity, kick off Prompt Surgeon isolation stage.
3) If high-impact and widespread, open incident ticket and include PS owner and SRE.
4) For automated canaries failing rollback, execute emergency rollback and notify customer success if customer-visible.

Ownership and Roles
-------------------
- Prompt Surgeon Owner: Applied ML Team (owner: Asha Menon).
- Evaluator / Replay Owner: Eval Harness Team (owner: Diego Alvarez).
- Production Canary & Deployment: Eng SRE (oncall rotation).
- Human reviewers: On-call applied-ml engineers + policy reviewer when applicable.

Example: Real-world case study (short)
------------------------------------
- Symptom: sudden 12% drop in structured-summary F1 on route /summarize at model v2.3.
- Isolation: cluster analysis showed regressions concentrated on templates that used trailing clarifying questions.
- Candidate: add anchor sentence "Summarize in three bullets, do not invent facts."
- Canary: 1% -> no control regressions, +9% F1 improvement, tokens +2%. Promoted after 48h.

Appendix A: Candidate Synthesis Pseudocode
------------------------------------------
- Pseudocode example (informal):
  1. for prompt in affected_prompts:
  2.   generate_paraphrases(prompt, limit=10)
  3.   for p in paraphrases:
  4.     if token_delta(p, prompt) <= 12:
  5.       run_shadow_eval(p)
  6.       compute_score(p)
  7. rank_candidates_by_score()

Appendix B: Example CLI snippets
--------------------------------
- Generate candidates locally:
  - redwood prompt-surgeon synth --prompt-id PROMPT-123 --limit 8 --seed 42
- Start a canary:
  - redwood prompt-surgeon canary --candidate PS-2025-0956 --percent 1 --duration 24h

Appendix C: Known Limitations and Future Work
---------------------------------------------
- Current approach targets surface-level prompt edits; it cannot safely rewrite prompts that fundamentally change task definition.
- Future: integrate compositional prompt repair (multi-edit planning), tighter integration with quantization-aware replays, and model-gradient-informed prompt sensitivity scores.
